learning_outcomes.text: Understand the structure of the vector space IR^n and the concepts of vector subspaces, linear dependence of vectors, basis, and dimension.
Apply the Gram-Schmidt method to obtain an orthonormal basis.
Solve and classify systems of linear equations.
Understand the notion of a matrix and master matrix algebra.
Calculate, interpret, and apply determinants of square matrices.
Identify linear functions (and matrices of linear functions) between vector spaces.
Calculate and interpret eigenvalues and eigenvectors. Diagonalize matrices. Determine integer powers of diagonalizable matrices.
Apply the singular value decomposition of a matrix to image compression.

syllabus_topics: Vectors and Systems of linear equations
Transpose and inverse of matrices. Properties.
Null and column space. The rank theorem.

assessment_methods.method: final exam (Assessment throughout the semester scheme)

assessment_rules: Students can choose between 'Assessment throughout the semester' or 'Exam assessment'. For 'Assessment throughout the semester', the final exam requires a minimum grade of 8.5 pts (out of 20), and the 4 best grades from the 5 written tests are considered. The final grade is the best between the two assessment schemes. The minimum grade for this course is 10 points (out of 20). The teaching team may require a supplementary assessment to validate work and verify knowledge acquisition, with its outcome being determinative.
